Icon button

A button that shows only an icon, for a familiar action where a text label has no room.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For a familiar action in a dense row or a toolbar, such as copying a branch name or opening a menu of more actions.
  • For a toggle that shows or hides part of the view, such as the terminal, with aria-pressed.

When not to use it

  • When the icon would not be understood without words. Use a button with a text label, with or without a leading icon.
  • For the main action of a view. Use a primary button with a text label.
  • To go to another view or another site. Use a link.
  • For a setting that is saved. Use a switch or a checkbox.

Variants

bordered
The default: ds-button ds-icon-button on one element. A standalone action that should read as a control.
quiet ds-button--quiet
ds-button ds-button--quiet ds-icon-button. No border until it is hovered or pressed, for a row or a toolbar that holds several.

Sizes

default
44px square, with a 16px icon. There is no smaller size: do not add ds-button--small, whose target would be narrower than 44px.

Accessibility

  • Use a button element with type="button", carrying ds-button and ds-icon-button. The icon is an svg with class ds-button__icon and aria-hidden="true".
  • The button must have an accessible name: an aria-label on the button, or text in a span with ds-visually-hidden inside it. The name is a verb and what it acts on, such as Copy branch name, and it names the item when the action repeats in a list, such as More actions for run 2184.
  • For a toggle, set aria-pressed="true" or "false" and switch it on each press. Keep the same name in both states: the state is announced from aria-pressed. The stylesheet adds a border, a sunken fill and a bar under the icon while it is on.
  • Disabled, aria-disabled and aria-busy behave as on the button. While busy, the spinner takes the place of the icon and the name says what is happening, such as Copying branch name.
  • Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the button element.
  • A tooltip may repeat the name for sighted readers, and is never the only place the name lives.
